visible_labels: Use {PREFIX} for the record type (RUN, TRN, INC and so on), {YYYY} or {YY} for the year, {GROUP} for the station or group (G followed by its ID, which must be followed by -, _ or .), and {SEQ} for the sequence, which is required. Letters, digits, -, _ and . are kept as written. The sequence restarts whenever the text around {SEQ} changes: including the year restarts it every year, and leaving out {PREFIX} gives every record type one shared sequence.

Digits in the SEQ part of the number pattern, zero-padded: 4 writes 0184. 3 to 8 digits; changing it keeps each sequence's next number. Department definitions with their own numbering keep their own width.

Month the numbering year starts, for records numbered by a fiscal year such as a county's or state's. Sequences that include the year start again at 1 on that month and day, and YYYY and YY write the fiscal year's name. Unset is January, the calendar year. Separate from call numbering's year start. Records request numbers and the numbers of inspections, permits, occupancies, investigations and evidence follow the same year.

For records numbered by a fiscal year, your own or a county's or state's you report to, pick the day it starts. Numbers that include the year start again at 1 that day, and {YYYY} and {YY} write the fiscal year's name. Most fiscal years are named by the year they end in, so one starting November 1, 2026 is 2027. January 1 is the calendar year. Call numbers have their own year start on the Call Settings page. Records request numbers and the numbers of inspections, permits, occupancies, investigations and evidence follow the same year.

How record numbers are written for the built-in record types and incident reports, for example RUN-0153: fixed text plus the PREFIX, YYYY or YY, GROUP and SEQ tokens. PREFIX writes each record type's prefix: its default or the department's own, from "Record type prefixes". Changing the pattern never renumbers records already numbered. Until a pattern is saved, the screen shows the one the department has always used.

Use {PREFIX} for the record type (RUN, TRN, INC and so on), {YYYY} or {YY} for the year, {GROUP} for the station or group (G followed by its ID, which must be followed by -, _ or .), and {SEQ} for the sequence, which is required. Letters, digits, -, _ and . are kept as written. The sequence restarts whenever the text around {SEQ} changes: including the year restarts it every year, and leaving out {PREFIX} gives every record type one shared sequence.

Digits in the SEQ part of the number pattern, zero-padded: 4 writes 0184. 3 to 8 digits; changing it keeps each sequence's next number. Department definitions with their own numbering keep their own width.
